page: Amazon Web Services m6i.12xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor providing 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and SHA extensions. The instance includes no local instance storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent disk storage, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 19 Gbps.

Benchmark results show balanced general-purpose execution across compute and memory workloads. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 48,594.14 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 15,732.0, placing in the average tier relative to comparable instances. Cryptographic operations and vector-heavy execution perform exceptionally well, reflected in an encryption test score of 43,612.59 and strong ray tracing marks of 49,473.0 in Geekbench. In memory testing, uncached large-block reads attain 161.66 GB/sec alongside 68.54 GB/sec write bandwidth, supporting 45.27 million Redis SET operations per second and 41.0 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

Without hardware GPU acceleration, large language model performance varies by model scale. Small model generation hits 266.35 tokens per second, but heavy 70B parameter models fall into lower performance percentiles at 2.75 tokens per second. The server offers consistent dedicated compute capability without local storage overhead, making it suitable for enterprise application servers, mid-tier database deployments, containerized web clusters, and multi-threaded CI/CD environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m6i.12xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores, paired with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory at a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The configuration excludes onboard local storage, requiring network-attached storage, while providing 19 Gbps of baseline network throughput. Performance testing demonstrates solid mid-tier multi-threaded compute, supported by AVX-512 extensions that yield strong results in encryption and vector processing. With memory read bandwidth of 161.66 GB/sec, it manages high-volume transactional workloads effectively. The instance is suited for multi-tier enterprise applications, container orchestration, caching layers, and relational database hosting.
